cultural.vision_reason: A beaded bustle medallion with feather back-ornament used in Plains-style dance regalia; such beadwork and bustle ornaments are made and worn across Pueblo peoples including the Tewa, so this fits the claimed culture's material culture.

physical.title: regalia; back-ornament (upper); medallion
physical.summary: Upper back bustle and bustle medallion.  The bustle is constructed of sticks wrapped in tape and coloured string, with feathers and orange strips of synthetic material streaming at the ends.  The sticks are threaded together with cord.  A wooden block is used to attach the bustle to the body, with holes to receive the cord (shoelace) which will be used to tie the bustle to the body.  The wooden block also gets concealed by a bustle medallion, which is constructed of two layers of cardboard discs, which are decorated and layered, the smaller on the larger; and attached with shoelaces threaded through the two disc layers.  The smallest top layer disc is constructed beaded hide with a rhinestone in the centre; the beads are white, blue, yellow, orange and red.  The larger disc is constructed of a three-layer cardboard backing with maroon feathers mounted on the front. Part of an ensemble of powwow regalia.

cultural.vision_reason: This is a loom-beaded choker with a classic Plains-style geometric diamond pattern, made as part of contemporary powwow regalia. Beaded powwow regalia of this type is a widely practiced Native American craft form and plausible for a Tewa maker/wearer; nothing in the image contradicts the claim.

physical.title: regalia; choker
physical.summary: Beaded choker with hanging strip.  Loom beaded beadwork is white, blue, yellow, orange, and maroon; all sewn onto cotton backing.  hide/leather straps for tying around the neck sewn to either end and leather/hide fringe at the bottom of the hanging strip.  Part of an ensemble of powwow regalia.

cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a pair of loom-beaded armbands with a geometric diamond design, hide backing, and ties — a type of beadwork worn as part of contemporary powwow regalia. Such beadwork is made and worn by many Native American people, including Pueblo peoples like the Tewa, so it is plausible for the claimed group even though the design style is widely shared.

physical.title: regalia; arm-band
physical.summary: Beaded armbands with hide or leather ties.  Loom-beaded beadwork is white, blue, yellow, orange, and maroon; all sewn onto hide or leather backing. One end of each armband has the ties, the other end has holes to slip the ties through .  Part of an ensemble of powwow regalia.
